_why: ADR 0052's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
`FormMixture.reason` warned that returning the lowest value 'would pick
a form rather than answer the question' -- conditionally, with nothing
anywhere saying whether it did. `name_selected_form()` answers that.
The corpus test attached to this ADR is worth more than the table: it
was written to prove the pipeline currently returns hexokinase I out of
three forms, and it does not. The minimum is 2.3e-07 from a row with no
designator. The claim the function was built on was wrong, and the test

mutations.description: a value appearing under two forms names one of them anyway
mutations._note: Two forms reporting the same number is a coincidence the data cannot resolve. Naming one invents the distinction the module exists to preserve.

mutations.description: a value from no named form is reported as one
mutations._note: The inversion. Not coming from a named form is the outcome the warning hoped for; reporting it turns good news into a finding.
mutations.find: if any(v == selected_value for v in values)

mutations.description: the reason stops saying the warning was not hypothetical
mutations._note: The whole point of the field. `FormMixture.reason` says returning the lowest *would* pick a form; this says it did.
mutations.find: "The warning above is not hypothetical for this result: a form was "

mutations.description: the sibling designators are not listed
mutations._note: 'One of three forms' is a claim a reader cannot check without the other two.

mutations.description: a one-form mixture claims a sibling gene product
mutations._note: Defensive: a single-designator mixture must not produce '...and LDH is a different gene product' with an empty name.
